planting.note: Plant tubers 2-3 inches deep in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade in fall before the ground freezes.

directions: 'Purple Bird' is a richly colored spring fumewort selection bearing tubular, violet-purple flowers held well above mounds of finely cut, blue-gray foliage. Like other Corydalis solida forms it is a true spring ephemeral, pushing up early, flowering for several weeks, and then dying back completely to a dormant tuber by early summer, so pair it with ferns or hostas that will fill the space it vacates. Plant tubers in fall, 2-3 inches deep, in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade under deciduous trees, where it will slowly bulk up into a dense colony and self-seed over successive seasons. Leave the foliage undisturbed until it yellows naturally so the tuber can store enough energy for next year's bloom.

planting.note: Plant tubers 2-3 inches deep in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade in fall before the ground freezes.

directions: 'White Knight' offers pure white, spurred flowers over the same finely dissected, gray-green foliage typical of spring fumewort, giving a bright, clean accent among the more common pink- and purple-flowered Corydalis solida selections. It completes its entire above-ground cycle in a few weeks each spring, emerging, flowering, and setting seed before vanishing to a dormant tuber for the rest of the year, so mark its location or interplant it with later-emerging perennials. Set tubers in fall, about 2-3 inches deep, in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade beneath deciduous trees and shrubs. Given a position it likes, it will multiply by offset tubers and self-sown seedlings into a steadily thickening drift over the years.

common_name: Late Snow Japanese Star Primrose (Large White Fringed)

planting.note: Plant divisions in early spring before new growth or in early fall; like the species, 'Late Snow' is winter-dormant and disappears completely below ground from midsummer through late winter, so mark the planting site.

directions: Plant divisions in early spring, just before new growth emerges, into moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, and mark the spot since the clump disappears entirely below ground by midsummer. 'Late Snow' is a Japanese-raised selection of sieboldii prized for its unusually large, lacy, pure white flowers with deeply notched petal lobes, opening somewhat later in the spring sequence than many other sieboldii cultivars and extending the bloom season in a woodland primrose collection. The soft, crinkled foliage emerges alongside the flower stalks and persists only into early summer before the plant goes fully dormant, an adaptation that lets it dodge summer heat and dry shade. Divide congested clumps while dormant or just as new growth appears, since named sieboldii selections are propagated by division rather than seed to keep the cultivar true.

common_name: Momiji Bashi Japanese Star Primrose (Deeply Cut Pink-Striped)

planting.note: Plant divisions in early spring before new growth or in early fall; like the species, 'Momiji Bashi' is winter-dormant and disappears completely below ground from midsummer through late winter, so mark the planting site.

directions: Plant divisions in early spring, just before new growth appears, into moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, marking the site since the clump vanishes completely each summer. 'Momiji Bashi' takes its Japanese name, meaning roughly 'maple-leaf bridge,' from its intricately dissected petal lobes, which curve gently to give each flower a star-like, almost snowflake-cut outline rather than the simple rounded petals of most primroses. Its pale pink flowers are streaked with deeper pink in a pattern that varies from bloom to bloom and even within a single flower head, so no two plants display quite the same mix of pale and vivid pink. Divide congested clumps while dormant or just as new growth emerges, since this and other named sieboldii cultivars must be propagated by division to remain true to type.

common_name: Glorious Japanese Star Primrose (Large Flat White)

planting.note: Plant divisions in early spring before new growth or in early fall; like the species, 'Glorious' is winter-dormant and disappears completely below ground from midsummer through late winter, so mark the planting site.

directions: Plant divisions in early spring, just before new growth appears, into moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, and mark the planting site since the clump disappears entirely below ground each summer. 'Glorious' produces unusually full, rounded flower heads of large white blooms whose petals sit flat in a single plane rather than cupping, giving the flowers a cleaner, more open face than many older sieboldii selections. The crinkled, oval leaves emerge with the flower scapes in spring and die back to dormancy by midsummer, the same fleeting above-ground season shared by the wild species and its many Japanese-bred cultivars. Divide congested clumps carefully while dormant or just as new growth appears, since this selection is maintained by division rather than seed to keep its flower form consistent.
